pairs: Et præteriens Jesus vidit hominem cæcum a nativitate:
And Jesus, while passing by, saw a man blind from birth.
that he would be born blind?”
sed ut manifestentur opera Dei in illo.
but it was so that the works of God would be made manifest in him.
Me oportet operari opera ejus qui misit me,
I must work the works of him who sent me,
when no one is able to work.
As long as I am in the world,
I am the light of the world.”
When he had said these things,
and he made clay from the spittle,
et linivit lutum super oculos ejus,
and he smeared the clay over his eyes.
lava in natatoria Siloë (quod interpretatur Missus).
wash in the pool of Siloam” (which is translated as: one who has been sent).
Therefore, he went away and washed,
Itaque vicini, et qui viderant eum prius quia mendicus erat,
And so the bystanders and those who had seen him before, when he was a beggar,
Nonne hic est qui sedebat, et mendicabat?
“Is this not the one who was sitting and begging?”
but he is similar to him.”
Ille homo qui dicitur Jesus, lutum fecit:
“That man who is called Jesus made clay,
et unxit oculos meos, et dixit mihi:
and he anointed my eyes and said to me,
Vade ad natatoria Siloë, et lava.
‘Go to the pool of Siloam and wash.’
Adducunt eum ad pharisæos, qui cæcus fuerat.
They brought the one who had been blind to the Pharisees.
Erat autem sabbatum quando lutum fecit Jesus,
when Jesus made the clay and opened his eyes.
Iterum ergo interrogabant eum pharisæi quomodo vidisset.
Therefore, again the Pharisees questioned him as to how he had seen.
Lutum mihi posuit super oculos, et lavi,
“He placed clay over my eyes, and I washed,
And so certain Pharisees said: “This man,
Non est hic homo a Deo, qui sabbatum non custodit.
who does not keep the Sabbath, is not from God.”
Quomodo potest homo peccator hæc signa facere?
“How could a sinful man accomplish these signs?”
And there was a schism among them.
Therefore, they spoke again to the blind man,
Tu quid dicis de illo qui aperuit oculos tuos?
“What do you say about him who opened your eyes?”
Non crediderunt ergo Judæi de illo,
that he had been blind and had seen,
until they called the parents of him who had seen.
quem vos dicitis quia cæcus natus est?
whom you say was born blind?
Then how is it that he now sees?”
Scimus quia hic est filius noster,
“We know that this is our son
and that he was born blind.
But how it is that he now sees,
Hæc dixerunt parentes ejus, quoniam timebant Judæos:
His parents said these things because they were afraid of the Jews.
For the Jews had already conspired,
ut si quis eum confiteretur esse Christum,
so that if anyone were to confess him to be the Christ,
he would be expelled from the synagogue.
It was for this reason that his parents said:
Vocaverunt ergo rursum hominem qui fuerat cæcus,
Therefore, they again called the man who had been blind,
nos scimus quia hic homo peccator est.
We know that this man is a sinner.”
And so he said to them:
How did he open your eyes?”
Why do you want to hear it again?
numquid et vos vultis discipuli ejus fieri?
Do you also want to become his disciples?”
But we are disciples of Moses.
Nos scimus quia Moysi locutus est Deus;
We know that God spoke to Moses. But this man,
we do not know where he is from.”
The man responded and said to them:
In hoc enim mirabile est quia vos nescitis unde sit,
that you do not know where he is from,
and yet he has opened my eyes.
scimus autem quia peccatores Deus non audit:
And we know that God does not hear sinners.
sed si quis Dei cultor est,
But if anyone is a worshipper of God
A sæculo non est auditum quia quis aperuit oculos cæci nati.
From ancient times, it has not been heard that anyone has opened the eyes of someone born blind.
Unless this man were of God,
he would not be able to do any such thing.”
Audivit Jesus quia ejecerunt eum foras:
Jesus heard that they had cast him out.
And when he had found him,
“Do you believe in the Son of God?”
so that I may believe in him?”
et qui loquitur tecum, ipse est.
and he is the one who is speaking with you.”
And falling prostrate, he worshipped him.
In judicium ego in hunc mundum veni:
“I came into this world in judgment,
so that those who do not see, may see;
and so that those who see, may become blind.”
Et audierunt quidam ex pharisæis qui cum ipso erant,
And certain Pharisees, who were with him, heard this,
et dixerunt ei: Numquid et nos cæci sumus?
and they said to him, “Are we also blind?”
